options.a: Suggest an offer amount, since helping the buyer also helps close the sale
options.b: Avoid acting as the buyer's advocate and stay within the listing agency role
options.c: Share the seller's lowest acceptable price so the buyer can offer efficiently
options.d: Give a price opinion as long as the buyer has signed the agency disclosure form

distractorExplanations.a: Recommending an offer amount is buyer advocacy that conflicts with the listing agent's loyalty to the seller.
distractorExplanations.c: Revealing the seller's bottom line breaches the confidentiality duty owed to the seller client.
distractorExplanations.d: Signing an agency disclosure does not create buyer representation; the agent still represents only the seller.

nc-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Listing agents represent the seller; advocacy for a buyer requires a proper agency shift/disclosure. If allowed, the brokerage may properly create buyer agency with required disclosures.

options.a: Lacked consideration or a legal purpose
options.b: Made only an oral agreement to buy land
options.c: Later found a better deal on another home
options.d: Was induced by fraud or was a minor

distractorExplanations.a: A contract missing consideration or a legal purpose is void or unenforceable, not voidable at one party's option.
distractorExplanations.b: An oral land contract is unenforceable under the statute of frauds, which differs from being voidable.
distractorExplanations.c: Buyer's remorse is not a legal ground; a valid contract cannot be avoided because a better deal appears.

nc-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Fraud or lack of capacity can make a contract voidable by the protected party. Whether the contract is voidable depends on the circumstances.

options.a: Obtain the highest price by carrying out every seller instruction, lawful or not
options.b: Owe the buyer customer the same loyalty and confidentiality as the seller
options.c: Promote the seller's interests with loyalty, care, and obedience within the law
options.d: Guarantee the seller a closed sale at list price within the listing term

distractorExplanations.a: Obedience extends only to lawful instructions; a broker must refuse illegal directions such as discriminatory or fraudulent ones.
distractorExplanations.b: Confuses client and customer: a buyer customer is owed honesty and fair dealing, not the fiduciary loyalty owed to the seller client.
distractorExplanations.d: Fiduciary duties concern conduct (loyalty, care, obedience), not guaranteed outcomes; brokers cannot promise a sale or price.

options.a: Delivering the signed deed to the grantee
options.b: Recording the deed in the public land records
options.c: Having the deed acknowledged before a notary
options.d: Sending written notice to each adjoining owner

distractorExplanations.a: Delivery and acceptance transfer title between the parties, but they do not give the world constructive notice.
distractorExplanations.c: Acknowledgment is what makes a deed eligible for recording; the notice to the world comes from recording itself.
distractorExplanations.d: Notifying specific people gives them actual notice only; constructive notice to everyone comes from the public record.

options.a: Contract dates and times are critical and late performance may be a breach
options.b: Parties may still perform within a reasonable time after each stated deadline passes
options.c: The closing date is firm, but other contingency deadlines may slip
options.d: The offer expires if the seller does not accept it within 24 hours

distractorExplanations.b: That is the default rule when the clause is absent; time is of the essence makes the stated deadlines strictly enforceable.
distractorExplanations.c: The clause applies to all contract dates, including inspection, financing, and appraisal contingency deadlines.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses the clause with an offer's expiration term; time is of the essence governs performance deadlines in the contract.

options.a: Can adjust whenever the lender chooses, without caps
options.b: Adjusts with the margin while the index stays fixed
options.c: Changes only when the borrower refinances the loan
options.d: Can adjust based on an index plus margin, subject to caps

distractorExplanations.a: ARM changes follow a published index on set adjustment dates, and periodic and lifetime caps limit each change.
distractorExplanations.b: Reverses the terms: the margin is fixed for the loan's life, and the index is the variable part that moves.
distractorExplanations.c: A refinance replaces the loan with a new note; an ARM's rate resets on scheduled adjustment dates under the existing note.

options.a: Physical damage to the home from fire, wind, or other covered perils
options.b: Covered title defects and claims against ownership per the policy
options.c: Losses to the lender when the borrower defaults on the mortgage
options.d: Title defects that arise after the policy date from future owners' acts

distractorExplanations.a: That is hazard (homeowners) insurance; title insurance covers defects in ownership, not physical damage to the structure.
distractorExplanations.c: That is mortgage insurance (PMI or FHA MIP); a lender's title policy protects the lien's validity, not repayment.
distractorExplanations.d: Title insurance looks backward: it covers defects existing on the policy date, not problems created by later owners.

options.a: The seller's reason for selling and lowest acceptable price, even if the seller objects
options.b: The racial or religious makeup of the neighborhood, since it may affect desirability
options.c: Known latent defects or conditions that could significantly affect value or desirability
options.d: Obvious patent defects, while hidden latent defects are left for the buyer's own inspection

distractorExplanations.a: Seller motivation and bottom-line price are confidential client information, not material property facts a buyer must be told.
distractorExplanations.b: Commenting on a neighborhood's race or religion is steering under the Fair Housing Act, not a required material-fact disclosure.
distractorExplanations.d: Reverses the rule: known latent (hidden) defects are exactly what must be disclosed, because a buyer cannot readily discover them.

nc-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Material property defects and legally required disclosures must be shared, as required by law; confidential motivations may be protected.

options.a: The listing broker earns a commission during the term except when the seller personally finds the buyer
options.b: The listing broker is owed a commission if the property sells during the term, regardless of who finds the buyer
options.c: Any cooperating broker who is the procuring cause earns the commission, and the seller may list with other firms
options.d: The broker keeps any proceeds above the seller's stated net price as compensation for the sale

distractorExplanations.a: That describes an exclusive agency listing, where the seller keeps the right to sell on their own without owing a commission.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes an open listing, where only the procuring broker is paid and the seller may list with several firms.
distractorExplanations.d: That describes a net listing, which is restricted or banned in many places; it is a compensation method, not exclusive right-to-sell.

nc-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Exclusive right-to-sell typically protects the listing broker's commission if a sale occurs during the listing term (per the agreement).

options.a: Practicing law any time they fill in a standard form's blanks for a client
options.b: Permitted to draft custom clauses as long as the client signs a waiver
options.c: Practicing law if they draft novel legal clauses beyond authorized forms
options.d: Required to have the client's attorney approve each filled-in form first

distractorExplanations.a: Filling in approved standard forms is generally permitted for licensees; drafting new legal language is what crosses into law practice.
distractorExplanations.b: A client waiver does not authorize a licensee to practice law; drafting novel legal clauses remains unauthorized practice.
distractorExplanations.d: Attorney review may be advisable or a contract contingency, but it is not a general prerequisite to completing standard forms.

options.a: Curtesy
options.b: Survivorship
options.c: Homestead
options.d: Descent to heirs

distractorExplanations.a: Curtesy is a husband's historic marital interest in a deceased wife's property, not a feature of joint tenancy.
distractorExplanations.c: Homestead protects a residence from certain creditors; it is a separate exemption, not a joint tenancy right.
distractorExplanations.d: Passing a share to heirs is a tenancy in common trait; in joint tenancy a deceased owner's share goes to the survivors.

options.a: Land bordering a still lake, sea, or ocean
options.b: Water use based on first in time, first in right by permit
options.c: Land bordering flowing water such as a river or stream
options.d: Ownership of subsurface minerals beneath a parcel of land

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses riparian with littoral rights, which apply to land bordering lakes, seas, and oceans rather than flowing water.
distractorExplanations.b: That describes the prior appropriation doctrine, a contrasting permit system, not riparian rights tied to bordering land.
distractorExplanations.d: Subsurface rights cover minerals and can be severed; riparian rights concern use of water by land bordering a stream.

options.a: 1% of the purchase price
options.b: 1% of the down payment
options.c: 1% of the loan amount
options.d: 1% of the interest rate

distractorExplanations.a: Points are computed on the loan amount, not the price; on a $200,000 price with a $160,000 loan, one point is $1,600.
distractorExplanations.b: Uses the wrong base: the down payment is the buyer's equity, while points are a percentage of the amount borrowed.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses one point (1% of the loan amount) with one percentage point of interest rate; a point typically buys down far less.

options.a: Originate new loans directly to borrowers at closing
options.b: Insure lenders against borrower default on high-LTV loans
options.c: Buy and sell existing mortgages, improving liquidity
options.d: Set the discount rate that member banks pay the Fed

distractorExplanations.a: That describes the primary mortgage market, where lenders originate loans; the secondary market buys loans already made.
distractorExplanations.b: That is the role of private mortgage insurance or FHA insurance, not the secondary market's buying and selling of loans.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses the secondary market with the Federal Reserve, which sets the discount rate as a monetary-policy tool.

nc-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-m.explanation: Entities like Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac (and others) buy existing loans, improving liquidity for originators so they can lend again.

options.a: When the first offer is drafted, even if the relationship began earlier
options.b: At closing, when the final settlement statement is reviewed and signed by both parties
options.c: Before or as soon as practicable when the dual/designated relationship arises
options.d: Within five days after the purchase contract is accepted by the seller

distractorExplanations.a: Waiting until an offer is written is too late if the dual or designated relationship already arose at a showing or earlier.
distractorExplanations.b: Disclosure at closing is too late; consent must be informed before the dual or designated relationship affects negotiations.
distractorExplanations.d: Invents a post-acceptance grace period; disclosure comes before or as soon as practicable when the relationship arises, not after acceptance.

nc-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Agency disclosure timing is early—when the dual or designated relationship is created or contemplated. Follow the applicable state agency-disclosure rules for the exact form and timing.

options.a: The broker is paid a flat fee no matter what price the property sells for
options.b: The broker's commission is a percentage split with the buyer's agent
options.c: The seller pays the broker only if the broker personally finds the buyer
options.d: The broker's compensation is the amount above a seller's net price

distractorExplanations.a: Describes a flat-fee listing; in a net listing the broker keeps whatever exceeds the seller's net figure, which creates the conflict.
distractorExplanations.b: Describes a cooperative commission split, which is common and lawful; a net listing pays the broker the excess over the seller's net.
distractorExplanations.c: Describes an exclusive agency listing, where the owner may sell without paying; it is unrelated to net-price compensation.

nc-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Net listings can incentivize underpricing relative to the seller's interests and are banned or tightly regulated in many places. That structure creates conflict-of-interest concerns because the broker profits from a low net figure.

options.a: A right of first refusal to match any offer the owner later accepts
options.b: An obligation to purchase on the stated terms whenever the optionor decides to sell
options.c: A right to purchase on stated terms within a period, usually for consideration
options.d: Equitable title to the property as soon as the option is signed

distractorExplanations.a: A right of first refusal lets the holder match a third-party offer; an option fixes the price and terms in advance.
distractorExplanations.b: The optionee has a right, not an obligation; the optionor is the party bound to sell if the optionee exercises the option.
distractorExplanations.d: Equitable title arises under a land contract or accepted purchase contract; an unexercised option conveys no ownership interest.

options.a: A misstatement of measurable fact that is excused if made in good faith
options.b: A statement of opinion that creates an express warranty the seller must honor
options.c: Exaggerated opinion that a reasonable person would not treat as a factual warranty
options.d: Prohibited advertising that the Commission treats like a material misrepresentation

distractorExplanations.a: A false statement of measurable fact is misrepresentation, not puffing; good faith may reduce fraud liability but does not make it opinion.
distractorExplanations.b: Puffing is the opposite of a warranty; a reasonable buyer would not rely on hype such as 'best view in town' as a guarantee.
distractorExplanations.d: The Commission disciplines misrepresentation of facts; general sales opinion that no reasonable person relies on is not treated as fraud.

options.a: Proceed as a dual agent, since written consent can be obtained after closing
options.b: Not create the dual agency relationship; consider designated agency, referral, or withdrawal
options.c: Proceed as a dual agent if the buyer consents, since one party's consent is enough
options.d: Represent the buyer and treat the seller as an unrepresented customer under the same listing

distractorExplanations.a: Dual agency consent must be informed and obtained before acting for both sides; it cannot be cured retroactively after closing.
distractorExplanations.c: Both principals must consent to dual agency; the buyer's consent alone does not authorize the broker to represent both sides.
distractorExplanations.d: The firm already owes the seller agency under the listing; it cannot drop that client to switch sides without a proper release.

options.a: Moving trust money into personal funds to use for the broker's own expenses
options.b: Holding several clients' deposits together in one pooled trust account
options.c: Mixing client trust money with personal or operating funds improperly
options.d: Depositing earnest money late, after the required deposit deadline has passed

distractorExplanations.a: Using trust funds for personal purposes is conversion, a more serious act than commingling, which is mixing without necessarily spending.
distractorExplanations.b: Pooling multiple clients' funds in a single trust account is permitted with proper ledgers; commingling mixes trust and broker funds.
distractorExplanations.d: A late deposit violates trust-account timing rules but is not commingling, which is mixing trust money with personal or operating funds.

options.a: Public use and the owner's written consent
options.b: Public use and payment of assessed value
options.c: Just compensation and a zoning variance
options.d: Public use/purpose and just compensation

distractorExplanations.a: Eminent domain is involuntary; the government may condemn without the owner's consent if public use and just compensation exist.
distractorExplanations.b: Just compensation means fair market value, not the tax-assessed value, which can differ substantially from market value.
distractorExplanations.c: A zoning variance is relief from zoning rules, unrelated to takings; eminent domain requires public use and just compensation.

nc-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Takings require public purpose and just compensation under the Constitution. This is the Fifth Amendment takings framework, applied to the states.

options.a: Upon the death of the remainderman
options.b: Upon the death of the measuring life
options.c: Upon the life tenant's sale of it
options.d: When the life tenant stops occupying it

distractorExplanations.a: The remainderman's death does not end a life estate; it is measured by the life tenant's (or named person's) life, and the remainder passes to heirs.
distractorExplanations.c: A life tenant may convey the interest, but the buyer receives an estate pur autre vie that still ends at the original measuring life's death.
distractorExplanations.d: A life tenant need not occupy the property; non-occupancy does not terminate the estate, which ends at the measuring life's death.

nc-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Life estates are measured by a life; remainder/reversion follows. The deed may define the measuring life as the grantee or another person (pur autre vie).

options.a: A gap in the chain of title that has been cured by quiet title
options.b: A zoning restriction that limits the property's permitted uses
options.c: A physical defect in the structure that the seller must disclose
options.d: A claim, encumbrance, or defect that may impair marketability

distractorExplanations.a: Once a quiet title action resolves the claim, the cloud is removed; a cloud is an unresolved claim that impairs marketability.
distractorExplanations.b: Public land-use controls such as zoning are not clouds on title; a cloud is a private claim or defect affecting ownership.
distractorExplanations.c: Physical condition issues belong in property disclosures; a cloud on title concerns ownership claims, not structural condition.

options.a: May hold unequal shares and typically lack survivorship unless specified
options.b: Must acquire title at the same time through the same deed
options.c: Hold equal shares and have survivorship unless the deed states otherwise
options.d: Cannot sell or will their share without consent of the other co-owners

distractorExplanations.b: Unities of time and title are joint tenancy requirements; tenants in common can acquire interests at different times by different deeds.
distractorExplanations.c: Reverses the defaults: equal shares and survivorship are joint tenancy features; tenants in common may hold unequal shares without survivorship.
distractorExplanations.d: A tenant in common may sell, mortgage, or devise an undivided interest freely without the other co-tenants' consent.

options.a: Permission to deviate from a zoning requirement due to hardship
options.b: A use allowed in a zone only after a special permit review
options.c: Permanent change of the zoning map for an entire district
options.d: A use that predates the ordinance and may continue as nonconforming

distractorExplanations.b: Describes a conditional (special) use permit for a use the ordinance allows with conditions; a variance relieves a hardship.
distractorExplanations.d: Describes a legal nonconforming use (grandfathered); a variance is a permitted deviation granted for a hardship.
distractorExplanations.c: That is rezoning/amendment.

nc-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Variances grant relief from strict zoning application in hardship cases. The variance is granted by the zoning authority (e.g., a board of adjustment).

options.a: Interest only for the term, with principal due as a balloon at maturity
options.b: Equal principal portions each month, so the interest portion stays level
options.c: Both interest and principal so the balance declines over the term
options.d: Mostly principal early in the loan and mostly interest near the end

distractorExplanations.a: Describes an interest-only (term) loan with a balloon payment; an amortizing loan retires principal with each payment.
distractorExplanations.b: Reverses the mix: on a level payment, the interest portion falls and the principal portion grows over the life of the loan.
distractorExplanations.d: Backwards: early payments are mostly interest because the balance is highest; the principal share grows toward maturity.

options.a: Prohibiting lending discrimination based on race, religion, sex, or marital status
options.b: Requiring APR disclosure and a right of rescission on certain refinance loans
options.c: Banning certain kickbacks and requiring settlement cost disclosures in covered transactions
options.d: Requiring lenders to report mortgage application data by census tract to detect redlining patterns

distractorExplanations.a: Lending discrimination is barred by the Equal Credit Opportunity Act and Fair Housing Act; RESPA targets settlement costs and kickbacks.
distractorExplanations.b: APR disclosure and the right of rescission come from the Truth in Lending Act (Regulation Z), not RESPA's kickback and settlement rules.
distractorExplanations.d: Describes the Home Mortgage Disclosure Act (HMDA); RESPA bans kickbacks and requires settlement cost disclosures.

options.a: Requires extra payment if the borrower pays off early, when the note allows it
options.b: Requires extra payment if the borrower makes a payment more than 15 days late
options.c: Lets the lender demand full payoff if the borrower sells the property
options.d: Lets the borrower pay off early with no charge, when the note allows it

distractorExplanations.b: Describes a late charge triggered by a missed due date; a prepayment penalty applies when the loan is paid off ahead of schedule.
distractorExplanations.c: Describes a due-on-sale (alienation) clause; a prepayment penalty is a charge for paying the loan off early.
distractorExplanations.d: Describes a prepayment privilege (open) clause, the opposite of a penalty; a prepayment penalty adds a charge for early payoff.

options.a: An FHA loan is made with a 3.5% down payment
options.b: Conventional LTV is high (commonly above 80%)
options.c: A VA loan is made with zero down payment to a veteran
options.d: Conventional LTV is low (commonly below 80%)

distractorExplanations.a: FHA loans carry FHA mortgage insurance premiums (MIP), not private mortgage insurance; PMI is a conventional-loan product.
distractorExplanations.c: VA loans have no monthly mortgage insurance; the VA guaranty and funding fee take its place, so PMI does not apply.
distractorExplanations.d: Reverses the threshold; PMI is triggered when the conventional LTV exceeds 80%, and borrowers at or below 80% LTV usually avoid it.

options.a: The buyer is credited; it reduces the cash needed to close
options.b: The seller is charged the item and the buyer receives an equal credit
options.c: The buyer is charged; it increases cash needed
options.d: The item is paid outside closing and shown only for disclosure

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses debit with credit: a buyer credit (such as earnest money or seller concessions) lowers the cash needed to close.
distractorExplanations.b: Describes a double entry between buyer and seller (such as a proration in the buyer's favor); a buyer debit is a charge to the buyer.
distractorExplanations.d: POC (paid outside closing) items are noted but not charged at the table; a debit is an amount the buyer must pay at closing.

nc-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-m.explanation: Debits charge a party; buyer debits typically increase funds due at closing. For the seller, a debit reduces sale proceeds.

options.a: Lending discrimination based on race, sex, or marital status
options.b: Maximum interest rates that may be charged on certain loans
options.c: Kickbacks and referral fees among settlement service providers
options.d: Minimum disclosures of loan costs such as the APR to borrowers

distractorExplanations.a: Credit discrimination is barred by the Equal Credit Opportunity Act; usury laws limit how much interest a lender may charge.
distractorExplanations.c: Kickbacks and unearned referral fees are prohibited by RESPA Section 8; usury laws address maximum interest charges.
distractorExplanations.d: Cost disclosure such as APR is governed by the Truth in Lending Act (Regulation Z), not usury laws, which cap the interest rate.

options.a: Refinance an existing home to lower the rate over a new 30-year amortizing term
options.b: Fund construction in stages through draws, then convert to a permanent loan once the home is finished
options.c: Finance a short-term gap, often between purchase of a new home and sale of an existing one
options.d: Combine a first mortgage and a second loan to avoid PMI on a new home purchase

distractorExplanations.a: A rate-and-term refinance is long-term permanent financing; a bridge loan is short-term and repaid when the old home sells.
distractorExplanations.b: Describes a construction-to-permanent loan with staged draws; a bridge loan is a short-term gap loan tied to a home sale.
distractorExplanations.d: Describes a piggyback (80-10-10) loan structure used to avoid PMI, not a temporary gap loan between two homes.

options.a: Criminal penalties only, with no license action
options.b: Civil liability to the client, with no license action
options.c: License suspension/revocation proceedings
options.d: Discipline by the local REALTOR® association, not the Commission

distractorExplanations.a: A criminal conviction can also trigger separate administrative discipline by the NC Real Estate Commission against the license.
distractorExplanations.b: Civil exposure does not preclude discipline; the North Carolina Real Estate Commission can suspend or revoke for relevant convictions.
distractorExplanations.d: A REALTOR® association can enforce its ethics code but cannot suspend a state license; that power belongs to the NC Real Estate Commission.

nc-real-estate-readiness-check-nc-licens.explanation: Criminal convictions can trigger disciplinary cases. Proceedings are brought before the North Carolina Real Estate Commission.

options.a: Allowed if the ad includes the agent's phone number
options.b: Allowed when the licensee is selling their own home
options.c: Allowed on social media but not in print advertising
options.d: Prohibited or restricted by advertising rules

distractorExplanations.a: A phone number alone does not disclose that the advertiser is a licensee or identify the firm, so the ad is still a blind ad.
distractorExplanations.b: Licensees selling their own property must still disclose licensed status in advertising; owning the property does not exempt them.
distractorExplanations.c: Advertising rules apply to all media, including social media and websites; blind ads are prohibited online as well as in print.

options.a: Covers intentional fraud claims as well as negligence claims
options.b: Replaces the duty to disclose known material defects
options.c: Protects the buyer against defects in the property title
options.d: May be required, but does not excuse license law violations

distractorExplanations.a: E&O policies exclude intentional or fraudulent acts; they cover negligent errors and omissions in professional services.
distractorExplanations.b: Insurance does not change disclosure duties; licensees must still disclose known material defects, and E&O merely funds defense of claims.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes title insurance; E&O insures the licensee or firm against negligence claims arising from professional services.

nc-real-estate-readiness-check-nc-licens.explanation: E&O manages negligence risk; it is not a license to violate the law. Coverage may be mandated by the state commission or expected under firm risk practices.

options.a: Subject to advertising and inducement rules
options.b: Prohibited under RESPA as illegal kickbacks
options.c: Exempt from regulation if offered to sellers
options.d: Allowed without disclosure if the prize is legal

distractorExplanations.b: RESPA kickback rules target settlement service referrals, not a broker's advertised inducement to a seller; state rules govern.
distractorExplanations.c: Inducements to sellers fall within Commission advertising and conduct rules; offering to a seller instead of a buyer is not exempt.
distractorExplanations.d: A lawful prize must still be advertised clearly and accurately, including all conditions; nondisclosure can be misleading advertising.

nc-real-estate-readiness-check-nc-licens.explanation: Inducements are regulated; deceptive or prohibited prizes can trigger discipline. They may be restricted or require clear disclosure of all conditions.

options.a: The broker-in-charge's written approval
options.b: MLS approval before the change is posted
options.c: Seller authorization (typically written)
options.d: Notice to the seller within five days

distractorExplanations.a: The broker-in-charge supervises but cannot set the seller's price; list price changes require the seller's own authorization.
distractorExplanations.b: The MLS records changes but does not approve them; the seller as principal decides the list price.
distractorExplanations.d: After-the-fact notice is not authority; the agent must have the seller's authorization before changing the list price.

nc-real-estate-readiness-check-nc-licens.explanation: Price is the seller's decision; agents need authority to change list price. Authorization follows the listing agreement and brokerage policy.

options.a: Permitted for any licensee, since REALTOR® is a generic term for agents
options.b: Permitted while a membership application with the local board is still pending
options.c: Improper trademark/membership misuse and can also be deceptive advertising
options.d: Improper only if the licensee also holds a broker license from the state

distractorExplanations.a: REALTOR® is a registered collective membership mark of NAR, not a generic job title; nonmembers may not use it.
distractorExplanations.b: Use of the mark begins once membership is approved; a pending application does not authorize advertising as a REALTOR®.
distractorExplanations.d: License level is irrelevant; the problem is claiming association membership the licensee does not have, whatever license is held.

options.a: Late fees, inactive status, or other penalties until cured
options.b: Immediate permanent revocation with no path to reinstatement
options.c: A grace period with full active status and no added fees
options.d: A requirement to retake the full prelicensing course and exam

distractorExplanations.b: Late renewal leads to expiration and reinstatement steps, not permanent revocation, which is a disciplinary sanction for misconduct.
distractorExplanations.c: There is no penalty-free grace period; an unrenewed license expires and cannot be used for brokerage until reinstated with fees.
distractorExplanations.d: Retaking prelicensing education and the exam applies after an extended lapse, not to a routine late renewal cured by fees and CE.

options.a: Disclose the defect only if a buyer asks directly
options.b: Advise the seller to check 'No Representation'
options.c: Follow the seller's instruction since the seller is the client
options.d: Refuse to conceal legally required disclosures

distractorExplanations.a: In North Carolina the duty to disclose known material facts is affirmative; waiting for the buyer to ask is still concealment.
distractorExplanations.b: A seller's No Representation choice on the NC disclosure statement does not relieve the broker of the duty to disclose known material facts.
distractorExplanations.c: Loyalty to the client does not extend to unlawful acts; a broker must refuse instructions to conceal a material fact.

nc-real-estate-readiness-check-nc-licens.explanation: Licensees cannot participate in fraud; illegal instructions must be refused. If the seller persists, the licensee should consider withdrawing from the listing.

options.a: Allowed if the listing agent is told afterward
options.b: Acceptable for a vacant listing only
options.c: Improper and a security/agency violation risk
options.d: Acceptable if the friend is a licensed appraiser

distractorExplanations.a: After-the-fact notice does not authorize access; showings require the seller's and listing broker's permission and a licensee present.
distractorExplanations.b: Vacancy does not lower the standard; unauthorized access to a vacant home still exposes the seller to theft, damage, and liability.
distractorExplanations.d: Professional status does not grant access; even an appraiser must enter by appointment authorized through the listing broker.

options.a: Acceptable puffing because square footage is an opinion
options.b: Only a problem if the buyer relied on it and closed the sale
options.c: A material misrepresentation that can trigger discipline and civil liability
options.d: An error the seller alone is liable for, since the seller supplied the figure

distractorExplanations.a: Square footage is a measurable fact, not opinion; misstating it knowingly is willful misrepresentation, not puffing.
distractorExplanations.b: Commission discipline does not require a closed sale or buyer damages; knowingly misstating square footage is itself a violation.
distractorExplanations.d: The prompt says the licensee knew better; a broker who passes along figures known to be wrong is personally liable.

options.a: Share the main office's broker-in-charge instead of naming their own
options.b: Use a separate trade name without registering it with the Commission
options.c: Be registered/comply with branch office rules when required
options.d: Keep a separate trust account at each branch location

distractorExplanations.a: In North Carolina each office, including a branch, must have its own designated broker-in-charge supervising that location.
distractorExplanations.b: A firm using an assumed business name must register it, and the name must not mislead the public into seeing a separate firm.
distractorExplanations.d: Branch offices are not required to hold their own trust account; the firm's trust accounting and supervision rules still apply.
